Subject: New vendor onboarding — invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Dev,

Thanks for helping with the onboarding. We're kicking off setup for Acme's resale contract and need to confirm your invoice ingestion expectations so we can align our AP system. A few quick items:

- Do you require invoices to be submitted via your portal (preferred) or is email PDF accepted as a fallback?
- If portal-first, what are the required fields and filename conventions so our exports map cleanly to PO lines?
- Are multi-PO invoices allowed (one PDF with multiple PO references)? If so, how should line items be formatted?

I've attached a sample invoice and our current template. Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Oliver —

Great to meet you virtually. TL;DR: portal-first, email fallback accepted with constraints. Details below so you can pass to your AP team.

1) Portal (preferred)
- Please register via our vendor onboarding form (see attached vendor_onboarding_form.pdf) and follow the portal invitation link. Portal submissions are tokenized and auto-acked; they guarantee PO matching and faster payment processing.
- Required fields: PO number, Vendor legal entity, Invoice date, Invoice number, Currency, Line item description, Quantity, Unit price, Tax amount, Total.
- Filename convention: REDWOOD_<PO>_<INVNUM>_YYYYMMDD.pdf (this helps our ingestion idempotency).

2) Email fallback (acceptable during transition)
- Send to invoices@redwood.com with subject: "Invoice: <VendorName> <PO> <Invoice#".
- PDFs only; one invoice PDF per message preferred. If you must submit a bundled PDF with multiple PO references, include a cover page with a clear table of PO -> page ranges. Bundled PDFs increase manual triage time and may delay payment.

3) PO stamping and multi-PO rules
- We support multi-PO invoices, but each PO must have clearly delimited line ranges and matching totals. If totals don't reconcile per PO, the entire invoice is routed to manual review.

4) Acknowledgements and headers
- Portal: immediate ack with token and ingestion id.
- Email: we return an automated ack within 24 hours when subject and filename conventions are followed. For email-submitted invoices that fail auto-parse, please expect a short follow-up from our AP ops team asking for a corrected file or CSV breakdown.

Attachments: acme_invoice_template_v2.xlsx (we'll use this to validate your export). I've CC'd Monica (vendor ops) and Ben (AP lead) to steer the onboarding checklist.

Next steps:
- Oliver: confirm whether Acme can export to the filename convention and whether you expect multi-PO bundles.
- We'll send a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones (portal invite, test invoice, production go-live).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Sr. Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Oliver / Acme team —

Appreciate the follow-ups. Answers and decision summary below so we can lock the onboarding MAP: 

1) Combined/batched PDFs
- Acceptable with cover page PO -> page map. Please ensure each PO section includes a PO subtotal matching your ERP. If the PO subtotal mismatches our PO record, the invoice will go to manual review (this is the main delay vector).

2) Header label tolerance
- Parser is tolerant to common header label variations ("PO#", "Purchase Order", "P.O."), but we recommend standardizing to one label in your export to reduce edge cases. We'll run a single test invoice through ingestion prior to go-live.

3) Filename extension with batch id
- Including the batch id is fine — keep the base convention at the front: REDWOOD_<PO>_<INVNUM>[_BATCHxxx]_YYYYMMDD.pdf. The parser looks for the PO and INVNUM tokens first.

Action items (owners):
- Oliver: send a sample batch export (PDF) and a CSV of the same set by Tue 04/06 for validation (Acme).
- Ben: run a test ingestion once sample is received; report parsing exceptions back to Acme.
- Monica & Lauren: create the MAP entry and a short onboarding checklist (portal invite, test invoice, 2-week post-go-live check).

We will treat the portal as the long-term canonical path and keep email as a supported transitional flow. If parsing exception rate exceeds 8% for email-submitted files for two consecutive weeks, we will request prioritized portal usage to avoid payment delays.

I'll follow up with the MAP link and a HubSpot deal update.

Best,
Dev Patel
Sr. Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference
